answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a per-identity collateral bond: every agent locks native stake to mint one identity, and if it splits into fake personas to farm rewards, dispute voters slash the entire bond. Running a thousand clones therefore needs a thousand bonds, so the attacker's cost scales linearly while payout per fake stays flat. That stake is a cipher only its owner can sign, a pigment marking each identity, and any duplicate falls into a slashable canyon. The attacker loses locked capital, not merely CPU time.
